title: Belonging in crisis: A mixed‐methods exploration of school disruption among marginalized girls in India
abstract: Abstract School closures can disrupt not only educational access but also the relational and institutional conditions through which adolescents experience school belonging. This sequential mixed‐methods study examined how COVID‐19–related school closures reshaped school belonging among marginalized adolescent girls in rural India. Guided by bioecological systems theory and intersectionality, we integrated surveys administered in 2021 ( N = 90) and 2022 ( N = 60) with two waves of focus group discussions. School belonging was conceptualized as a multidimensional, ecological, and relational experience reflected in peer and teacher connection, recognition, perceived fit, opportunities for agency, and aspirational attachment to school. Findings showed that belonging was increasingly constrained as closures continued. Girls reported growing household responsibilities, gendered restrictions on digital access, weakened contact with teachers, and heightened exposure to early marriage discussions; reported family conversations about marriage increased from 2% in 2021 to 20% in 2022. Sibling relationships, particularly girls' accounts of brothers' authority over household labor and phone access, revealed how broader gender norms were enacted within everyday family interactions. At the same time, peer relationships, teacher recognition, memories of residential school life, and educational aspirations sustained girls' connection to school despite prolonged physical absence. Girls consistently contrasted school as a space of relational connection, agency, and future possibility with home environments characterized by greater gendered constraints. The findings demonstrate that school belonging during crisis is dynamically produced across individual, relational, structural, and temporal contexts and underscore the importance of gender‐transformative approaches to educational continuity and post‐crisis recovery.
